title: FDA approves new drug treatment for chronic weight management, first since 2014
journal: US Food and Drug Administration, news release, 4 June 2021
result: FDA approved Wegovy (semaglutide 2.4 mg once weekly) for chronic weight management in adults with a BMI of 30 kg/m2 or more, or 27 or more with at least one weight-related condition, with a reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity; it was the first drug approved for chronic weight management in general obesity or overweight since 2014. Semaglutide 1 mg (Ozempic) had been approved for type 2 diabetes in 2017. Approval rested on four 68-week trials, three placebo-controlled and one randomised withdrawal trial, with more than 2600 patients on Wegovy and more than 1500 on placebo; placebo-adjusted weight loss was 12.4% in adults without diabetes and 6.2% in adults with type 2 diabetes. Labelled warnings at approval included thyroid C-cell tumours, pancreatitis, gallbladder disease, hypoglycaemia, acute kidney injury, diabetic retinopathy, increased heart rate and suicidal behaviour or thinking. Wegovy had not been studied in patients with a history of pancreatitis.
